title: File:XBio illustration – crRNA.png
desc: Also known as the “CRISPR RNA,” a piece of RNA transcribed from the CRISPR locus that contains one spacer from that locus. The crRNA therefore contains the “targeting sequence” that allows the Cas9 nuclease complex to identify a complementary piece of DNA at which it should make a cut.

title: File:NHGRI-97218.jpg
desc: CRISPR-Cas9 is a customizable tool that lets scientists cut and insert small pieces of DNA at precise areas along a DNA strand. The tool is composed of two basic parts: the Cas9 protein, which acts like the wrench, and the specific RNA guides, CRISPRs, which act as the set of different socket heads.

title: File:XBio illustration – TracrRNA.png
desc: Also known as the “trans-activating crRNA”, tracrRNA is a longer piece of RNA (compared to crRNA) that contains a constant sequence and provides the “stem loop” structure that is bound by the CRISPR nuclease (Cas9 in many cases).

title: File:XBio illustration – Cas Genes.png
desc: “CRISPR-associated” (Cas) genes express proteins that are involved in an immune response that protects bacteria against viruses (bacteriophage). title: File:XBio illustration – Prime Editing.png
desc: A modified version of CRISPR-Cas9 gene editing. In this method, a fusion protein consisting of a catalytically impaired Cas9 enzyme and reverse transcriptase is used to directly and specifically rewrite specific genomic sequences.

title: File:XBio illustration – Genome Editing.png
desc: A process by which a specific nucleotide or nucleotide sequence in a genome is changed. Now widely used with CRISPR–Cas9 for genetically engineering organisms and with potential applications to treat disease.
